**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most buyers.** Every source I found agrees on that. NMC only makes sense if weight matters most and you rarely use the unit.

## How they compare

| | LiFePO4 | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| **Cycle life** | Typically 3,000-6,000 cycles | Often 500-2,500, depending on the source |
| **Safety / heat** | More thermally stable, and it doesn't release oxygen when overheated | Less stable, with a higher thermal runaway risk |
| **Weight** | Heavier | Lighter, but by less than you'd expect |
| **Price** | Median about $0.55/Wh in one dataset | Median about $0.95/Wh in the same dataset |

- **Cycle life:** At one full cycle a day, 500 cycles lasts about 1.4 years and 3,000 cycles lasts about 8 years ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). If you cycle the unit only weekly or monthly, cycle life matters much less.
- **Weight:** At the cell level NMC is clearly denser. In finished stations, the inverter, case and fans weigh the same either way. One database found the median NMC unit only about 10% lighter per pound ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Another found about 16% ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Some LFP units are lighter per Wh than some NMC ones, so compare the actual specs.
- **Availability:** Most major brands have moved to LFP, and NMC is mostly in legacy or small models ([PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Cycle ratings:** Claims vary by brand and by end point (80% vs 70% capacity), so check both numbers.

## Picks

- **Longevity and home backup:** [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is LiFePO4 with 2,073.6 Wh and 6,000+ cycles to 80%. It weighs 24.2 kg. It's $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF (tested 10/24).
- **Smaller LiFePO4:** [BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) has 1,152 Wh and 3,500+ cycles, at $499 for the station alone ($474.05 with AFF5OFF). The $599 option is a bundle with a solar panel.
- **Budget LiFePO4:** [ALLPOWERS P1800](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-1024wh) has 1,024 Wh at about 13 kg, for $439 ($395.10 with ALLPOWERS26). Its 3,000 cycles are rated to 70%, not 80%. The page contradicts itself on some specs, and the warranty is 24 months.
- **Weight matters most (NMC):** [ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-s2000-pro-1451wh) has 1,451 Wh and 2,400 W in 13 kg, with 2,500+ cycles. It's $664, or $597.60 with EXTRA10, which expires 11/15. Its solar input spec conflicts (1,000 W in the spec table, 650 W in the FAQ).

After codes, the S2000 Pro and the Elite 200 V2 both come to about $0.41/Wh, so NMC isn't cheaper per Wh here ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/portable-power-station-lifepo4-nmc-battery-chemistry-manufacturer-comparison-202)).

The buy links are Dealectric affiliate links, so they earn a commission at no cost to you. Promo codes were tested on the dates above and may change.

If you tell me your use (home backup, van, camping) and budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
